summary: Almost every element of LocProd(T) is a unit, and such an element of R that is not a unit of R is divisible, at some w ∈ T, by the uniformiser ϖ_w; so R ∖ R^× ⊆ ⋃_{w∈T} {x : ϖ_w⁻¹x ∈ R} up to a null set. Each of these sets has measure md(ϖ_w⁻¹)⁻¹ = q_w⁻¹ ≤ b(S)⁻¹⁰ (q_w is a level prime), and #T ≤ 2·#(chosen places) = 4f(E) ≤ b(S)/250, whence the bound b(S)⁻⁹.

steps.claim: 1000 ≤ b(S) (the field thousand_le_b of the filling data).

The first claim, 2 ≤ b(S)⁹, follows from 1000 ≤ b(S) (bound: 2 ≤ 1000⁹). For the second, by monotonicity of the measure up to null sets it suffices that almost every x ∈ R ∖ R^× lies in ⋃_{w∈T} {x : ϖ_w⁻¹·x ∈ R} (ϖ_w the unit of LocProd(T) equal to the uniformiser at w and to 1 elsewhere): a.e. x is a unit of LocProd(T) (P.ae_isUnit); if no ϖ_w⁻¹x were integral, every component x_j would have valuation 1, so x ∈ R^×, a contradiction (simp_all with v(ϖ_j⁻¹x_j) ≤ 1 ⟺ v(x_j) < 1).

steps.claim: The numerical inequality 2·(2f(E))·b(S)⁻¹⁰ ≤ b(S)⁻⁹ (#chosenPlaces(S, i) = f(E) for i = 0, 1): after gcongr and clearing denominators it is 4f(E) ≤ b(S), which bound derives from f(E) ≤ b(S)/1000 (f_le_b).

Each set has measure vol{x : ϖ_w⁻¹x ∈ R} = md(ϖ_w⁻¹)⁻¹ = [ϖ_w⁻¹] (md = [·]⁻¹), and the generalised index is the product of the inverse norms of the components, of which only the w-component differs from 1: it is ‖ϖ_w‖_w = q_w⁻¹ (norm_locField_eq_q_zpow).
